blocks.content: Manipur's culture chapter is anchored by Manipuri classical dance — one of India's eight recognised classical dance forms — alongside the state's claim to being the birthplace of modern polo and its rich, ethnically diverse festival calendar.

Manipuri dance is one of the eight officially recognised classical dance forms of India (alongside Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Sattriya and Mohiniyattam), directly rooted in the Vaishnavite devotional culture that took hold following King Garibniwaz's 18th-century conversion (Chapter 2).

The Raas Leela is the most celebrated form of Manipuri dance, a devotional dance-drama depicting episodes from the life of Krishna and Radha, characterised by gentle, flowing, restrained movements (in contrast to the more percussive footwork of several other classical Indian dance forms), graceful circular formations, and distinctive costume — notably the ornate, cylindrical 'Kumil' skirt worn by female dancers.

Manipuri dance's global recognition owes much to the patronage and popularisation efforts of Rabindranath Tagore, who encountered the form during a visit to Manipur/Sylhet in the early 20th century and subsequently incorporated it into the curriculum at his institution, Visva-Bharati University (Santiniketan), helping introduce the form to a wider Indian and international audience.

★ EXAM POINT: Manipuri dance is distinguished among India's 8 classical dance forms by its GENTLE, non-percussive, flowing movement style and its DIRECT Vaishnavite-Krishna-devotional (Raas Leela) content — and by Rabindranath Tagore's specific role in popularising it via Santiniketan, a frequently tested culture-history crossover fact.

Manipur is widely credited as the birthplace of modern polo, based on the traditional indigenous game 'Sagol Kangjei' (a Manipuri horseback stick-and-ball game with ancient roots), which British colonial officers and soldiers encountered in Manipur in the 19th century and subsequently adapted, codified and exported globally as the modern sport of polo.

The Manipur Polo Club, founded in the 1850s, is cited by polo historians as one of the oldest polo clubs in the world, reinforcing Manipur's claim to being the game's original home — a frequently cited sporting-history fact for the state.

★ EXAM POINT: 'Sagol Kangjei' = the traditional Manipuri game credited as the origin of modern polo; the Manipur Polo Club (founded 1850s) is cited as one of the world's oldest polo clubs — a distinctive sporting-heritage fact for this state.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Yaoshang (Meitei) and Kut (Kuki-Zo) are the two most frequently tested named community-specific festivals of Manipur; the Sangai Festival is the modern, government-organised, pan-community tourism showcase event, distinct from these older traditional community festivals.

items: Manipuri dance = one of India's 8 classical dance forms; Raas Leela (Krishna-Radha devotional dance-drama) is its most celebrated form; popularised nationally/internationally by Rabindranath Tagore via Santiniketan.
'Sagol Kangjei' = traditional Manipuri game credited as the origin of modern polo; Manipur Polo Club (1850s) = one of the world's oldest polo clubs.
Yaoshang (Meitei, Feb-Mar) and Kut/Chavang Kut (Kuki-Zo, November) are major community-specific harvest/festive traditions.
Sangai Festival = modern, government-organised, statewide tourism festival, named after the Sangai deer.
